name: Cincinnati
operatingHours: The Connector streetcar runs a 3.6-mile downtown/Over-the-Rhine loop Mon–Fri 7:30 AM–11:30 PM, Sat 8:30 AM–11:30 PM and Sun 9:30 AM–9:30 PM, every ~12–15 min; extended hours for some events.
fareInfo: The Connector streetcar is free to ride (no ticket needed). Metro buses and TANK buses (Northern Kentucky, incl. the CVG airport bus) are $2 a ride; a Metro/TANK 1-Day Pass is $5, payable in the Transit app (EZfare) or with exact cash.

sights.name: Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden
sights.note: One of America's oldest zoos (1875), known for its hippo Fiona, the Africa savanna and lush botanical gardens; seasonal evening light shows.
sights.hours: ~10:00 AM–5:00 PM daily (evening events in Oct and Nov–Dec)

sights.name: Cincinnati Museum Center
sights.note: Art Deco Union Terminal (1933) with a famous half-dome rotunda, housing natural history, Cincinnati history and children's museums; Amtrak still stops here.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–5:00 PM daily; to 8:00 PM select Fridays

sights.name: Great American Ball Park
sights.note: Riverfront home of the Cincinnati Reds, baseball's oldest pro franchise; offseason behind-the-scenes tours.
sights.hours: MLB season late Mar–Sep (game times vary); offseason ballpark tours on select dates

sights.name: American Sign Museum
sights.note: A warehouse full of glowing neon and hand-painted signs from a century of American storefronts, with a recreated 'Main Street'.

sights.name: Krohn Conservatory
sights.note: Art Deco glasshouse in Eden Park with rainforest, desert and orchid rooms plus seasonal flower and butterfly shows.
sights.hours: Tue–Sun 10:00 AM–5:00 PM, closed Mon (timed tickets for the butterfly show)

sights.name: Findlay Market
sights.note: Ohio's oldest continuously operated public market (1855): butchers, bakeries, goetta, and a weekend farmers market in Over-the-Rhine.
sights.hours: Tue–Fri 9:00 AM–6:00 PM, Sat 8:00 AM–6:00 PM, Sun 10:00 AM–4:00 PM, closed Mon

sights.name: National Underground Railroad Freedom Center
sights.note: Riverfront museum on the Underground Railroad and the fight against slavery, including a 19th-century slave pen moved from Kentucky.

sights.name: Roebling Suspension Bridge
sights.note: John Roebling's 1866 blue suspension bridge to Covington, Kentucky, a forerunner of his Brooklyn Bridge; walk it for skyline views.

sights.name: Smale Riverfront Park
sights.note: Riverfront park between the stadiums with fountains, a carousel, swings, gardens and the Ohio River walk.

sights.name: Spring Grove Cemetery & Arboretum
sights.note: A vast 19th-century garden cemetery and national historic landmark, with lakes, champion trees and grand monuments.
sights.hours: Grounds ~8:00 AM–6:00 PM daily (longer in summer)

sights.name: Fountain Square
sights.note: Downtown's central plaza around the 1871 Tyler Davidson Fountain, with concerts in summer and an ice rink in winter.

sights.name: Cathedral Basilica of the Assumption
sights.note: Gothic Revival basilica in Covington, Kentucky, modelled on Notre-Dame and Saint-Denis, with one of the world's largest stained-glass windows.
sights.hours: Open daily, roughly 9:00 AM–4:00 PM outside Mass times

sights.name: Eden Park
sights.note: Hilltop park above the Ohio River with Mirror Lake, overlooks and the Cincinnati Art Museum and Krohn Conservatory.

sights.name: Cincinnati Reds Hall of Fame & Museum
sights.note: Interactive museum of Reds history next to the ballpark, from the 1869 Red Stockings to the Big Red Machine and Pete Rose's hit wall.
sights.hours: Oct–Mar: Tue–Sun 10:00 AM–5:00 PM (closed Mon and Bengals home Sundays); season: daily 10:00 AM–5:00 PM, later on game days

sights.name: William Howard Taft National Historic Site
sights.note: Birthplace and boyhood home of the 27th president and later chief justice, restored to the 1850s, in Mount Auburn.
sights.hours: Grounds 9:00 AM–4:00 PM daily; house tours when the education center is open

sights.name: Cincinnati Music Hall
sights.note: An 1878 Victorian Gothic concert hall facing Washington Park, home to the symphony, pops, opera and ballet.
sights.hours: Open for performances; guided tours on select days

sights.name: Washington Park
sights.note: Over-the-Rhine's lively green, with a splash pad, dog park, bandstand and free events, surrounded by bars and restaurants.

sights.name: Cincinnati Art Museum
sights.note: Free museum in Eden Park with 67,000 works, from Egyptian antiquities to Rookwood pottery and a Van Gogh.
sights.hours: Tue–Sun 11:00 AM–5:00 PM, Thu to 8:00 PM, closed Mon; general admission free

railStations.name: Cincinnati Union Terminal
railStations.note: Amtrak's Cardinal (3x weekly) to Chicago (~9h) and to Washington DC (~15h) and New York (~19h), in the Art Deco Cincinnati Museum Center. About 2 km west of downtown and not on the streetcar; take Metro bus 1 or a taxi.
railStations.hours: Trains call in the small hours: to Chicago ~2:20 AM Mon/Thu/Sat, to Washington/New York ~3:35 AM Wed/Fri/Sun. Station waiting room opens only around train times.

airports.name: Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport
airports.transitNote: In Hebron, Kentucky, ~20 km south-west of downtown and not on the streetcar. TANK bus 2X Airporter runs to downtown (5th & Vine/Government Square) every ~30 min in ~25–45 min for $2; taxi or rideshare ~20–25 min.
airports.hours: 2X from the terminal: first ~4:25 AM, last regular trip ~1:00 AM (plus one ~3:00 AM trip).
